raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview On SM100, prefer Humming over Marlin for dense int4 symmetric group-128 weights. Extends #56997 (SM90); roadmap #61024. ## Claims - 3.1x faster 4k prefill on `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4`, decode unchanged. - `vllm bench serve`: TTFT 2.6-3.6x lower and TPOT flat at concurrency 1/8/32 ([raw results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63561#issuecomment-6412985534)). - Group-32/zero-point weights keep Marlin, where Humming decodes 5-6% slower. ## Test Plan ```text pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py -> 27 passed, 1 skipped LLM(RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4) -> Using HummingLinearKernel for mixed-precision linear LLM(cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4) -> Using MarlinLinearKernel for mixed-precision linear ``` Decode step = (T(out=128) - T(out=1)) / 127 at 128 input tokens; 2 interleaved rounds, spread < 0.5%. | Qwen3.8-27B, 1xB200 | Marlin (main) | Humming | |---|---|---| | INT4 g128 sym, prefill 4k | 555.5 ms | **179.6 ms** | | INT4 g128 sym, decode bs1 / 8 / 32 | 8.15 / 8.72 / 12.00 ms | 8.11 / 8.71 / 12.12 ms | | AWQ g32 asym, decode bs1 / 8 / 32 | 8.30 / 8.89 / 12.20 ms | 8.83 / 9.38 / 12.78 ms | ## Details MoE and other formats unchanged; SM103 untested. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

nodes.body: @jinzhen-lin this PR extends #56997 to SM100, but only for int4 symmetric group-128 dense weights; with group 32 and zero points Humming was 5-6% slower at decode on B200, so those keep Marlin. Could you take a look? cc @mgoin

@chaunceyjiang `vllm bench serve`, 1xB200, `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4`, PR branch: `--linear-backend marlin` (main's pick) vs `auto` (Humming). Random dataset, median of 2 interleaved rounds (spread ≤ 2%).

| in / out | conc | out tok/s (Marlin → Humming) | mean TTFT ms | mean TPOT ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024/1024 | 1 | 118.4 → 120.2 | 159.8 → 62.3 | 8.3 → 8.3 |
| 1024/1024 | 8 | 802.2 → 863.1 | 1051.2 → 332.8 | 9.0 → 9.0 |
| 1024/1024 | 32 | 1922.0 → 2321.7 | 3923.8 → 1097.0 | 12.8 → 12.7 |
| 4096/128 | 1 | 78.2 → 101.7 | 581.1 → 194.4 | 8.3 → 8.4 |
| 4096/128 | 8 | 185.9 → 406.9 | 3992.2 → 1124.1 | 11.9 → 10.9 |
| 4096/128 | 32 | 215.9 → 586.8 | 8887.8 → 2658.6 | 79.3 → 33.9 |

TTFT is 2.6-3.6x lower in every cell; TPOT is flat except 4096/128 c32, where prefill chunks share steps with decode.

```text
vllm serve RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 --linear-backend {marlin,auto} --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len {4096,1024} --random-output-len {128,1024} --ignore-eos --num-prompts max(4*conc,16) --max-concurrency {1,8,32} --seed 0
```

files.patch:
@@ -26,18 +26,23 @@
     ScaledMMLinearKernel,
     TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel,
     _get_linear_backend,
+    _prefer_humming_on_sm100,
     _resolve_backend_kernels,
     init_fp8_linear_kernel,
     init_int8_linear_kernel,
     register_linear_kernel,
 )
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mixed_precision.MPLinearKernel import (
+    MPLinearLayerConfig,
+)
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.humming import prioritize_humming
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import (
     kFp8Dynamic128Sym,
     kFp8Static128BlockSym,
     kFp8StaticTensorSym,
 )
 from vllm.platforms import PlatformEnum
+from vllm.scalar_type import scalar_types
 
 pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
 
@@ -422,3 +427,44 @@ def test_humming_priority_only_reorders_humming_and_marlin(possible_kernels):
     del names[humming]
     assert names == [k.__name__ for k in original if "Humming" not in k.__name__]
     assert kernels == original
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "weight_type,group_size,zero_points,expected",
+    [
+        (scalar_types.uint4b8, 128, False, True),
+        (scalar_types.uint4, 32, True, False),
+        (scalar_types.uint4, 128, True, False),
+        (scalar_types.uint4b8, 32, False, False),
+        (scalar_types.uint8b128, 128, False, False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_humming_priority_sm100_mixed_precision(
+    weight_type, group_size, zero_points, expected
+):
+    """SM100 moves Humming directly ahead of Marlin only for int4 symmetric
+    group-128 weights; no other kernel moves and other devices are unchanged."""
+    kernels = _POSSIBLE_KERNELS[PlatformEnum.CUDA]
+    original = list(kernels)
+    config = MPLinearLayerConfig(
+        full_weight_shape=(5120, 5120),
+        partition_weight_shape=(5120, 5120),
+        weight_type=weight_type,
+        act_type=torch.bfloat16,
+        group_size=group_size,
+        zero_points=zero_points,
+    )
+
+    assert _prefer_humming_on_sm100(kernels, config, 103) == original
+    reordered = _prefer_humming_on_sm100(kernels, config, 100)
+    assert kernels == original
+    names = [k.__name__ for k in reordered]
+    humming = names.index("HummingLinearKernel")
+    marlin = names.index("MarlinLinearKernel")
+    assert (humming == marlin - 1) == expected
+    if not expected:
+        assert reordered == original
+    del names[humming]
+    assert names == [
+        k.__name__ for k in original if k.__name__ != "HummingLinearKernel"

issue_comments.body: @jinzhen-lin this PR extends #56997 to SM100, but only for int4 symmetric group-128 dense weights; with group 32 and zero points Humming was 5-6% slower at decode on B200, so those keep Marlin. Could you take a look? cc @mgoin

@chaunceyjiang `vllm bench serve`, 1xB200, `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4`, PR branch: `--linear-backend marlin` (main's pick) vs `auto` (Humming). Random dataset, median of 2 interleaved rounds (spread ≤ 2%).

| in / out | conc | out tok/s (Marlin → Humming) | mean TTFT ms | mean TPOT ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024/1024 | 1 | 118.4 → 120.2 | 159.8 → 62.3 | 8.3 → 8.3 |
| 1024/1024 | 8 | 802.2 → 863.1 | 1051.2 → 332.8 | 9.0 → 9.0 |
| 1024/1024 | 32 | 1922.0 → 2321.7 | 3923.8 → 1097.0 | 12.8 → 12.7 |
| 4096/128 | 1 | 78.2 → 101.7 | 581.1 → 194.4 | 8.3 → 8.4 |
| 4096/128 | 8 | 185.9 → 406.9 | 3992.2 → 1124.1 | 11.9 → 10.9 |
| 4096/128 | 32 | 215.9 → 586.8 | 8887.8 → 2658.6 | 79.3 → 33.9 |

TTFT is 2.6-3.6x lower in every cell; TPOT is flat except 4096/128 c32, where prefill chunks share steps with decode.

```text
vllm serve RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 --linear-backend {marlin,auto} --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len {4096,1024} --random-output-len {128,1024} --ignore-eos --num-prompts max(4*conc,16) --max-concurrency {1,8,32} --seed 0
```
